# ApkUp — Complete Documentation & Knowledge Base (v1.46.0 / Build 231)

> ApkUp is a free, ad-free, open-source (GPL-3.0) Android app updater for Android 10.0 – 17 (API 29+). It unifies Google Play, F-Droid Index V2, IzzyOnDroid, APKMirror, GitHub Releases, GitLab Releases, Codeberg Releases, and Direct APK URLs with automatic SHA-256 & signing-certificate verification, Obtainium JSON import, and optional silent background updates via Shizuku or Root (su).

- Website: https://durcheins.github.io/apkup/
- Repository: https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup
- Latest Signed APK & SHA256SUMS: https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/releases/latest
- Supported ABIs: arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64
- Minimum Android Version: Android 10.0 (API 29) up to Android 17


---

## Key Differentiators (ApkUp vs. Obtainium vs. Aurora Store vs. F-Droid)

- **8+ Update Sources in One App:** Google Play Store, F-Droid Index V2 (official & custom repos with SHA-256 verification), IzzyOnDroid, APKMirror, GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, and Direct APK URLs.
- **No Root Required for Background Updates:** Supports standard Android PackageInstaller, optional Shizuku (no root), and optional Root (`su`), with Wi-Fi-only and charging-only rules.
- **Play Store Version Checking Without Play Account:** Checks Play Store updates via Aurora / GPlay API integration with intelligent fallback across sources.
- **Hardware-Backed Credential Storage:** GitHub/GitLab/Codeberg Personal Access Tokens (PATs) are encrypted using Google Tink (AES-256-GCM) backed by Android Keystore and strictly host-isolated.
- **100% Obtainium JSON Import & Live Checker:** Import existing Obtainium JSON configs directly into ApkUp with automatic source mapping.
- **Signing-Certificate & SHA-256 Protection:** Verifies APK signatures and checksums before installation to prevent downgrade or spoofing attacks.


---

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Do I need Root for silent background updates?
No. ApkUp supports Shizuku out of the box, which grants elevated PackageInstaller permissions on stock Android (Android 11+ via Wireless Debugging or ADB) without rooting your device. Optional Root (su) is also supported for users who already run rooted devices or want single-tap in-place rollbacks.

### Does Google Play Store checking require my Google account?
No. ApkUp uses anonymous session tokens from the community Aurora Dispenser together with a privacy-minimized device compatibility profile (CPU ABI, Android SDK, density, and language) to fetch compatible updates without any personal login.

### How does ApkUp protect me from tampered or incompatible APKs?
Before any installer runs, ApkUp cryptographically verifies APK Signature Scheme v2/v3 certificates against the installed app, validates SHA-256 digests and signed F-Droid indexes, blocks version downgrades, checks minSdk/ABI compatibility, and isolates .apkm extraction against Zip-Slip and decompression bombs.

### Can I migrate my tracked apps from Obtainium or App Watcher?
Yes. ApkUp includes an interactive Obtainium JSON import preview (for app bindings, custom F-Droid repos, and watchlist candidates) as well as Obtainium JSON export and direct App Watcher watchlist import.

### How do ApkUp self-updates and the Beta channel work?
ApkUp checks official GitHub releases (stable-only by default) and validates SHA256SUMS digests plus signing certificates before updating itself. Under Setup → About, you can opt into the Beta channel at any time and cleanly return to stable on opt-out.

### Does ApkUp collect any analytics, crash logs, or telemetry?
Zero. ApkUp has no developer backend, no ads, no analytics SDKs, and no telemetry. First-launch source consent ensures zero network requests run until you choose your sources, and preferences/tokens are encrypted at rest with Google Tink (AES-256-GCM).

---

## Privacy Policy

# Privacy Policy for ApkUp

**Last Updated:** November 13, 2026

ApkUp is an open-source, client-side Android application developed by DurchEins. This Privacy Policy explains how ApkUp handles data and respects user privacy.

---

### 1. No Developer Backend, Analytics, or Ads
ApkUp is designed with a strict **Privacy by Design** philosophy:
- **No Developer Servers:** There is no ApkUp backend, proxy server, or developer database logging user queries or IP addresses.
- **No User Accounts Required:** ApkUp does not require registration, login, or user profiles.
- **No Analytics or Telemetry:** ApkUp contains zero analytics SDKs, crash trackers, or behavioral telemetry (no Google Firebase, no Crashlytics, no Sentry, no Mixpanel).
- **No Advertisements:** ApkUp is completely free of ads, tracking banners, and ad networks.
- **No Hardware Identifiers:** ApkUp never collects or transmits IMEI numbers, hardware serial numbers, MAC addresses, or Advertising IDs.

---

### 2. Explicit Source Consent & Network Activity
On first launch, ApkUp presents a **Choose Update Sources** consent dialog. No external network checks are performed until you choose which sources to enable, and you can toggle any source on or off at any time in Settings:

- **F-Droid & IzzyOnDroid (Signed Repository Indexes):** Downloads signed repository index archives (`index-v1.jar` / `entry.json`) via HTTPS from `f-droid.org`, `apt.izzysoft.de`, or custom HTTPS F-Droid mirrors you add, and compares versions locally on your device. Your list of installed apps is **not** transmitted to F-Droid or IzzyOnDroid.
- **GitHub, GitLab & Codeberg / Forgejo:** Queries public release endpoints (`api.github.com`, `gitlab.com`, `codeberg.org`, or user-configured self-hosted GitLab/Forgejo hosts) via HTTPS solely for installed or user-watched apps mapped to open-source repositories. Optional Personal Access Tokens are sent strictly to their respective host and never forwarded across cross-host redirects.
- **APKMirror:** Queries `www.apkmirror.com` via HTTPS (API and/or public RSS/Atom feeds) to check version numbers and resolve APK download links for tracked packages.
- **Google Play Store (Anonymous Compatibility Check):** When enabled, ApkUp requests an anonymous session token from the community Aurora Dispenser (`auroraoss.com`) and queries `android.clients.google.com` via HTTPS using installed package IDs and a minimized device compatibility profile (CPU ABI, Android SDK version, screen density, and normalized language code) to retrieve compatible update metadata. No personal Google account is used.

---

### 3. Device Permissions & Encrypted Local Storage
ApkUp requests only standard Android permissions necessary for its core functionality:
- `INTERNET` & `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE`: Required to query enabled update sources and download APK files over HTTPS.
- `REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES`: Required to hand over verified APK packages to the Android system `PackageInstaller` or optional Shizuku service.
- `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`: Optional permission to notify you about available updates and download progress.
- `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`: Required locally on the device to inspect installed package names, version codes, and signing certificates so ApkUp can detect updates and block signature-mismatched packages before installation.
- `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` & `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC`: Used by AndroidX `WorkManager` to run user-initiated update downloads reliably.

All local settings, repository bindings, and optional API tokens are stored exclusively in private app storage encrypted at rest via **Google Tink (AES-256-GCM)** backed by the Android Keystore. Cloud backups and device-to-device data extraction are disabled (`android:allowBackup="false"`). Downloaded APK files are stored inside ApkUp's private internal cache directory (and automatically purged after installation or expiration) unless you explicitly use "Save APK" to export a copy to your chosen download folder. Any local diagnostic log (`AppJournal` + process logcat) stays strictly offline on your device, strips access tokens, and is only saved or shared when explicitly triggered by you.

---

### 4. Open Source Auditing
ApkUp is licensed under the **GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPLv3)**. Its entire source code is publicly accessible and open to independent security audits at:  
https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup

---

### 5. Contact
If you have any questions or concerns regarding this Privacy Policy, please reach out via GitHub:
- **Issue Tracker:** https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/issues
- **Security Advisories (Confidential):** https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/security/advisories/new

---

## Security Policy

<a id="top"></a>

# Security Policy

**Last Reviewed:** November 2026

> [!CAUTION]
> **Security vulnerabilities must NEVER be opened as public GitHub Issues, Discussions, or social media posts.**
> Disclosing unpatched issues publicly puts ApkUp users at risk. Use GitHub's confidential advisory workflow below instead.
>
> <a href="https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/security/advisories/new"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Report%20a%20Vulnerability-Private%20Advisory-DC2626?style=flat&logo=github" alt="Report a Vulnerability via Private Advisory" /></a>

## Supported Versions

We actively provide security patches for the following versions of ApkUp:

| Version | Support Status | Scope |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `1.46.x` (or newer) | ✅ **Full support** | Active bug fixes & security patches |
| `1.45.x` | ⚠️ **Security fixes only** | Critical security patches until next minor release |
| `< 1.45` | ❌ **Unsupported** | Please update to the latest release |

---

## 🔐 Official APK Signing Verification & Single-Artifact Principle

All official **ApkUp** releases follow the **Single-Artifact Principle**: only the release APK built, signed, and published by automated GitHub Actions (`release.yml`) is canonical. All official mirrors (**GitLab Releases**, **Zapstore**, **itch.io**, **APKPure**, **Appteka**, **Komi Store**) and VirusTotal scans distribute and verify this exact same binary.

Always verify that the signing certificate SHA-256 fingerprint matches ApkUp's official key before trusting an APK:

```text
8e9b512371ee965afc7cc91f23490d3a514623b90d483e638bba8a070a2170b4
```

Per-release `.sha256` checksum files (`SHA256SUMS`) are published alongside each release binary on **[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/releases)** and on the **[ApkUp Website](https://durcheins.github.io/apkup/)**.

---

## 🛡️ Security Architecture & Threat Model

ApkUp enforces defense-in-depth verification across every stage of checking, downloading, and installing updates:

| Layer | Protection Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- |
| **APK Integrity** | `ApkIntegrityVerifier` checks v2/v3 signing certificates against the installed app and blocks mismatches or version downgrades before handing files to `PackageInstaller`, Shizuku, or Root. |
| **Signed Indexes & Hashes** | F-Droid / IzzyOnDroid indexes (`index-v1.jar`) verify against pinned 64-hex SHA-256 X.509 fingerprints; self-updates verify against signed `SHA256SUMS`. |
| **Credentials at Rest** | Preferences and optional API tokens are encrypted locally via **Google Tink (`AES-256-GCM`)** backed by the hardware **Android Keystore**. |
| **Network & Redirects** | HTTPS-only transport (`cleartextTrafficPermitted="false"`). Personal Access Tokens are strictly host-isolated and stripped across cross-host redirects. |

<details>
<summary><b>🔍 Detailed Threat Model, Archive Limits &amp; Data Isolation</b></summary>
<br>

### Threat Model Defenses
- **Split-Bundle Hardening (`.apkm`):** Archive extraction enforces strict canonical path validation against **Zip-Slip** directory traversal as well as hard per-entry and total **decompression-bomb byte limits**.
- **UI & Process Protections:** Sensitive confirmation controls filter obscured touches against **Tapjacking**, external intents harden against Background Activity Launch (**BAL**) restrictions, and local diagnostic logs (`AppJournal`) scrub credentials automatically before export.
- **Privilege Boundaries:** Standard Android `PackageInstaller` requires explicit system confirmation; **Shizuku** runs via scoped ADB binder permissions; optional **Root (`su`)** execution performs explicit pre-checks on target package paths.

### Local Storage & Data Isolation
- **No Cloud Backups:** Cloud backup and device-to-device data extraction are disabled (`android:allowBackup="false"`).
- **Private Cache Isolation:** Downloaded APKs reside exclusively in private internal app storage (`cacheDir`) and are cleaned up automatically unless explicitly exported via *Save APK*.
- **Zero Telemetry:** ApkUp operates strictly client-side with zero analytics SDKs or developer servers. Full data handling details are documented in **[PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md)**.

</details>

---

## 📩 Reporting a Vulnerability

If you discover a potential security vulnerability in ApkUp (especially regarding APK signature checks, `.apkm` extraction, Shizuku IPC / optional Root `su` execution, token storage, or network transport), please report it privately via **[GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting](https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/security/advisories/new)**.

### What to Include in a Report
- **ApkUp version & Android OS version** (e.g., `1.45.2 (227)` on Android 15)
- **Affected component or update source** (e.g., `ApkIntegrityVerifier`, F-Droid index parser, Shizuku installer, Tink storage)
- **Step-by-step reproduction** or Proof-of-Concept (PoC)
- **Expected security impact** (e.g., signature bypass, arbitrary file write, credential leak)

- **Coordinated Disclosure Policy:** Best-effort acknowledgement within **7 days**; we kindly ask researchers to allow coordinated disclosure until a patched release is published (typically within **30–90 days**).

---

<details>
<summary><b>🇩🇪 Deutsche Zusammenfassung (German Summary)</b></summary>
<br>

> [!CAUTION]
> **Melde Sicherheitslücken NIEMALS als öffentliches GitHub-Issue!** Nutze immer vertraulich das **[private Meldeformular auf GitHub](https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/security/advisories/new)**.

### Unterstützte Versionen
| Version | Status | Hinweis |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `1.45.x` (oder neuer) | ✅ **Voller Support** | Aktive Bugfixes & Sicherheitsupdates |
| `1.44.x` | ⚠️ **Nur Sicherheitsfixes** | Kritische Sicherheitsupdates bis zum nächsten Minor-Release |
| `< 1.44` | ❌ **Nicht unterstützt** | Bitte auf die aktuellste Version aktualisieren |

### Offizieller Signatur-Fingerprint (SHA-256) & Single-Artifact-Prinzip
Nur die über GitHub Actions signierten Release-APKs auf **GitHub Releases** sind kanonisch (identische Binärdatei & Prüfsumme auf allen offiziellen Mirrors). Offizieller Zertifikat-SHA-256-Fingerprint:

```text
8e9b512371ee965afc7cc91f23490d3a514623b90d483e638bba8a070a2170b4
```

### Sicherheitsarchitektur im Überblick
- **Signatur- & Prüfsummenschutz:** `ApkIntegrityVerifier` prüft v2/v3-Signaturzertifikate vor jeder Installation und blockiert Downgrades sowie abweichende Signaturen; F-Droid-/IzzyOnDroid-Indizes und Selbst-Updates (`SHA256SUMS`) werden kryptografisch geprüft.
- **Verschlüsselte Speicherung & Datenisolierung:** Einstellungen und optionale Tokens liegen per **Google Tink (`AES-256-GCM`)** im Android Keystore verschlüsselt, Cloud-Backups sind deaktiviert (`allowBackup="false"`), Downloads liegen im privaten `cacheDir`. Weitere Details stehen in **[PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md)**.
- **Archiv-, Netzwerk- & UI-Härtung:** Schutz vor Zip-Slip und Entpackbomben bei `.apkm`-Bundles, ausschließlich HTTPS mit strikt host-isolierten Tokens, Tapjacking-Schutz und automatische Redaktion sensibler Daten in Diagnose-Logs.
- **Checkliste für Meldungen:** Bitte nenne betroffene ApkUp-/Android-Version, betroffene Komponente/Quelle, Reproduktionsschritte bzw. PoC und mögliche Auswirkungen.
- **Koordinierte Offenlegung (Coordinated Disclosure):** Best-Effort-Rückmeldung innerhalb von **7 Tagen**; wir bitten Sicherheitsforscher um eine koordinierte Offenlegung, bis ein gepatchtes Release veröffentlicht ist (üblicherweise innerhalb von **30–90 Tagen**).

</details>

## Wiki: Overview & Quick Start

# 📖 Welcome to the Official ApkUp Wiki

Welcome to the central knowledge base for **ApkUp** — an open-source, privacy-first Android app updater built with Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Material 3 Expressive.

Every main guide is structured into clear layers:
- 🟢 **Part 1 (Plain Language):** Everyday step-by-step instructions without technical jargon.
- 💻 **Part 2 (Technical Deep Dive):** Architecture, cryptography, Android Binder IPC, and security guarantees.
- ❓ **Part 3 (FAQ & Edge Cases):** Practical answers to common real-world questions.

---

## Wiki: Update Sources, Repository Linking & Signature Protection

# 🌐 Update Sources, Repository Linking & Signature Protection in ApkUp

This guide explains how ApkUp's update sources work together, how **Source Priority & Per-App Pinning** choose the best download, how **Pre-Release Channels** and **Signature Verification** protect your device, and how to link custom GitHub, GitLab, or Codeberg/Forgejo repositories.

> Looking for a specific error message (`HTTP 403`, `HTTP 429`, `DNS`, Cloudflare, or `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE`)? Jump straight to **[Troubleshooting Source Errors](https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/wiki/Troubleshooting-Source-Errors)**.

<a id="-part-1-explained-simply-for-everyone"></a>
## 🟢 Part 1: Explained Simply for Everyone

<a id="11-which-update-sources-does-apkup-search"></a>
### 1.1 Which update sources does ApkUp search?
ApkUp unites six independent update channels in a single interface. You can enable or disable each source individually in **Setup**:

| Source | Best For | Key Highlight in ApkUp |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Google Play Store** | Everyday mainstream apps | Works completely anonymously without signing into a personal Google account. |
| **APKMirror** | Fast rollouts before Play Store stages reach you | Verifies architecture, Android version, and signatures automatically with per-app Cloudflare cooldowns. |
| **F-Droid & IzzyOnDroid** | Free & Open-Source Software (FOSS) | Unified bottom sheet with Index V2 (`entry.jar` / `index-v1.jar`) verification, pre-pinned presets, and TOFU pinning for custom repos. |
| **GitHub** | Open-source apps straight from developers | Built-in catalog + custom repo bindings, optional regex asset filter, GraphQL batching, and token testing. |
| **GitLab** | Projects hosted on GitLab (Aurora Store, VLC, Briar) | Supports `gitlab.com`, self-hosted instances, and nested subgroups. |
| **Codeberg / Forgejo** | Community FOSS apps (e.g., Gadgetbridge) | Supports `codeberg.org`, self-hosted Forgejo instances, and optional access tokens. |

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="12-direct-in-app-downloads-from-apkmirror"></a>
### 1.2 Direct In-App Downloads from APKMirror
When **Direct APKMirror Downloads** is enabled under **Setup ➔ APKMirror**, ApkUp resolves the download link in the background, downloads the APK or `.apkm` bundle directly inside the app, and installs it without forcing you through ad-heavy browser pages.
- If Cloudflare triggers an interactive check, ApkUp opens a compact **in-app WebView** first and only falls back to your system browser if needed.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="13-what-is-an-app-signature-and-why-is-it-so-important"></a>
### 1.3 What is an "App Signature" and why does it matter?
Every Android app carries an invisible cryptographic seal from its developer — its **digital signature**.
- Android **only** allows an update if the new APK has the exact same signature as the installed app.
- **How ApkUp protects you:** ApkUp checks signatures during update discovery and again before installation (`minSdk`, `ABI`, and signing certificate), blocking tampered or mismatched updates before Android fails on them.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="14-multi-source-priority--per-app-pinning"></a>
### 1.4 Multi-Source Priority & Per-App Pinning
When an app offers updates on multiple sources simultaneously, ApkUp keeps your **Updates** list clean by showing each app once:
- **Global Source Priority:** Open **Setup ➔ Source Priority** and reorder sources via drag-and-drop or arrow buttons to choose your preferred default order.
- **Per-App Source Pinning:** In **Apps** or **Updates**, pin an individual app to a specific source (e.g., always prefer GitHub over Play Store). If the pinned source currently has no update, ApkUp automatically falls back to your global order.
- **Alternative Sources:** Tap any update card to view all other sources offering that update and switch with one tap.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="15-guide-linking-a-custom-github-gitlab-or-codeberg-project"></a>
### 1.5 Guide: Linking a Custom GitHub, GitLab, or Codeberg Project
1. Open the **Apps** tab and tap the desired app.
2. Select **Link Repository (GitHub / GitLab / Codeberg)**.
3. Paste the full repository URL or shorthand (`owner/repo` for GitHub/Codeberg, `group/subgroup/project` for GitLab, plus custom host if self-hosted).
4. Optionally add an **APK Asset Regex** (with live test preview) if the release ships multiple APK variants, then tap **Save**.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="-part-2-technical-documentation-for-experts--power-users"></a>
## 💻 Part 2: Technical Documentation for Experts & Power Users

<a id="21-parallel-multi-source-aggregation--version-verification"></a>
### 2.1 Parallel Multi-Source Aggregation & Version Verification
ApkUp queries all enabled sources concurrently and in isolation, so one slow or unreachable provider never blocks the others:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Installed["Local Package Scanner\n(Installed Apps + Certificates)"] --> Orchestrator["Update Aggregator\n(Source Priority & Pinning)"]
    
    Orchestrator --> Play["Google Play Store\n(Anonymous gplayapi)"]
    Orchestrator --> AM["APKMirror\n(REST v2 Batch API)"]
    Orchestrator --> FD["F-Droid / IzzyOnDroid\n(Index V2 + Diffs)"]
    Orchestrator --> GH["GitHub\n(REST / GraphQL)"]
    Orchestrator --> GL["GitLab\n(API v4 Releases)"]
    Orchestrator --> CB["Codeberg / Forgejo\n(API v1 Releases)"]
    
    Play & AM & FD & GH & GL & CB --> Dedupe["Deduplication, Signature\n& Compatibility Guard"]
    Dedupe --> UI["Updates Overview\n(Primary Card + Alternative Sources)"]
```

**Two-Stage Version Verification + Compatibility Guard:**
1. Strictly higher Android `versionCode` (when provided by the source) and semantic version progression.
2. Pre-install compatibility check verifying device `minSdk`, supported CPU `ABI`s, and signing certificates before launching installation.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="22-cryptographic-signature-verification-sha-1--sha-256--origin-detection"></a>
### 2.2 Cryptographic Signature Verification (SHA-1 & SHA-256) & Origin Detection
ApkUp computes both **SHA-1** and **SHA-256** signing fingerprints via `PackageManager` (`GET_SIGNING_CERTIFICATES` on API 28+):
- **APKMirror:** Strictly matches the remote SHA-1 fingerprint against the installed app.
- **F-Droid / IzzyOnDroid:** Matches the local certificate against the `signer` SHA-256 hash recorded in the repository index.
- **Install Origin Detection:** Uses `PackageManager.getInstallSourceInfo()` to flag cross-source signature mismatches proactively.
- **Local Export Exception:** When using **Save APK**, file/archive/SHA-256 integrity is verified without blocking export if the installed app uses a different signer.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="23-direct-apkmirror-resolution--hardened-apkm-split-extraction"></a>
### 2.3 Direct APKMirror Resolution & Hardened `.apkm` Split Extraction
1. **Three-Stage Link Resolution:** Variant page ➔ time-signed download page ➔ final CDN stream.
2. **Cooldown & Anti-Bot Handling:** Enforces per-app 10-minute cooldowns on failures, opens an in-app Cloudflare WebView when interactive verification is needed, and falls back to the system browser if still blocked.
3. **Hardened `.apkm` Extraction:** Inspects true ZIP structure (`AndroidManifest.xml` at root vs. embedded split `.apk`s), rejects Zip-Slip (`..` / path traversal) entries, and writes atomic `.part` downloads before finalizing.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="24-google-play-store-dispenser-resilience--http-429-recovery"></a>
### 2.4 Google Play Store Dispenser Resilience & HTTP 429 Recovery
Anonymous Play Store queries use shared guest sessions via Aurora Dispenser. On `HTTP 429`, ApkUp rotates the guest session in a synchronized manner with cooldown protection so concurrent downloads share the refreshed session without flooding the dispenser.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="25-three-tier-repository-resolution-for-github-gitlab--codeberg"></a>
### 2.5 Three-Tier Repository Resolution for GitHub, GitLab & Codeberg
1. **Priority 1 – Custom User Bindings:** Manually linked repositories (plus optional asset regex).
2. **Priority 2 – Built-in Project Catalog:** Curated package-to-repo mappings bundled with ApkUp.
3. **Priority 3 – Automatic Source Discovery & FOSS Flavor Heuristic:** Upstream URLs discovered from F-Droid/IzzyOnDroid indexes, preferring FOSS builds for F-Droid-origin apps and deprioritizing `-debug` / incompatible artifacts.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="-part-3-frequently-asked-questions-faq"></a>
## ❓ Part 3: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

<a id="31-why-does-apkup-show-a-warning-icon-for-a-signature-conflict"></a>
### 3.1 Why does ApkUp show a warning icon for a "Signature Conflict"?
Apps compiled by F-Droid use F-Droid's signing key, whereas GitHub or Play Store builds use the developer's or Google's key. Android forbids overwriting an app across different signing keys. Pick the matching source under **Alternative Sources**, or uninstall the existing app first if you want to switch signers.

<a id="32-do-i-need-a-google-account-for-play-store-updates"></a>
### 3.2 Do I need a Google account for Play Store updates?
**No.** ApkUp uses anonymous guest sessions and never asks for your personal Google credentials.

<a id="33-why-does-apkmirror-sometimes-open-an-in-app-webview-or-my-browser"></a>
### 3.3 Why does APKMirror sometimes open an in-app WebView or my browser?
APKMirror uses Cloudflare bot protection. When Cloudflare requires human verification, ApkUp opens an in-app WebView first (or falls back to your browser if running in the background) so you can still complete the download.

<a id="34-what-are-apkm-files-and-can-apkup-install-them-directly"></a>
### 3.4 What are `.apkm` files and can ApkUp install them directly?
Yes! `.apkm` files are split APK bundles (base app + language/ABI/density splits). ApkUp extracts and installs all matching splits automatically.

<a id="35-how-do-i-manage-alpha--beta-pre-releases-for-apps-and-apkup-itself"></a>
### 3.5 How do I manage Alpha / Beta pre-releases (for apps and ApkUp itself)?
* **For Tracked Apps:** Open **Setup ➔ Include Pre-Releases** to enable individual channels (**Beta**, **RC**, **Alpha**, **Nightly**) globally, or override pre-release behavior per app inside its details sheet. By default, pre-releases are disabled.
* **For ApkUp Itself (Self-Updater):** Open **Setup ➔ About ➔ Receive beta updates** (disabled by default) to opt into ApkUp pre-release builds. Turning it off automatically returns you to the stable track with the next regular release.

<a id="36-does-apkup-support-self-hosted-gitlab-and-forgejo-servers"></a>
### 3.6 Does ApkUp support self-hosted GitLab and Forgejo servers?
**Yes!** Both self-hosted GitLab (including nested subgroups) and self-hosted Forgejo instances over `https://` are supported when linking repositories.

## Wiki: F-Droid & Index V2 Repositories

# 📦 F-Droid & Index V2 Repositories in ApkUp

← Back to [Wiki Home](Home) · [Troubleshooting Source Errors](Troubleshooting-Source-Errors#8-f-droid--izzyondroid--codeberg--forgejo-issues)

Starting with **v1.40.0+**, ApkUp upgrades its F-Droid and community repository processing to the modern **F-Droid Index V2** specification (`index-v2.json`). This brings dramatic improvements in network efficiency, memory usage, and update accuracy.

---

## 📑 Quick Navigation

* [1. What is F-Droid Index V2?](#1-what-is-f-droid-index-v2)
* [2. Why the Upgrade from Index V1 (`index.xml`)?](#2-why-the-upgrade-from-index-v1-indexxml)
* [3. Supported Community Repositories](#3-supported-community-repositories)
* [4. Managing Built-in & Custom F-Droid Repositories](#4-managing-built-in--custom-f-droid-repositories-v1431)
* [5. Security, Signing Keys & Fingerprint Verification](#5-security-signing-keys--fingerprint-verification)

---

## 1. What is F-Droid Index V2?

The F-Droid Index V2 format is the next-generation metadata catalog for Android open-source repositories. Instead of relying on monolithic, memory-intensive XML archives, Index V2 distributes repository manifests formatted as streamlined JSON objects (`index-v2.json`), partitioned by application packages and cryptographic release signatures.

---

## 2. Why the Upgrade from Index V1 (`index.xml`)?

Prior to v1.40, repository metadata was parsed from legacy `index.jar` / `index.xml` feeds. This came with significant disadvantages on mobile devices:
* ⚠️ **High RAM & CPU Consumption:** Parsing a 30+ MB uncompressed XML file required tens of megabytes of heap allocation and could cause stutter on mid-range devices.
* ⚠️ **Slow Cold Checks:** Reading XML tags sequentially slowed down background checks.
* ⚠️ **Bandwidth Waste:** Entire catalogues had to be parsed even if only a few packages changed.

### The Index V2 Advantages in ApkUp:
* ⚡ **Streaming JSON Parser:** ApkUp streams `index-v2.json` directly from the network without allocating huge string buffers into RAM.
* ⚡ **Incremental Index-V2 Diffs & Caching:** Uses `ETag`, `Last-Modified`, and signed F-Droid Index-V2 diffs (`RFC 7396` JSON Merge Patch with mandatory SHA-256 verification) to download only lightweight incremental changes when your local cache is up to date, automatically falling back to the full `index-v2.json` when needed.
* ⚡ **Instant Package Matching:** Direct hashmap lookup matching your device's installed package names in milliseconds.

---

## 3. Supported Community Repositories

ApkUp connects natively with major verified repositories inside a single unified repository manager:
1. **IzzyOnDroid (`apt.izzysoft.de`):** The premier curated repository for open-source applications built directly from developer repositories with original developer signatures.
2. **Official F-Droid Repository (`f-droid.org`):** The global repository for free and open-source software built from source on F-Droid build servers.
3. **Built-in Verified Presets:** Ready-to-enable profiles for **NewPipe Repo (`archive.newpipe.net`)**, **microG Repo (`microg.org`)**, and **Guardian Project (`guardianproject.info`)** with pre-pinned SHA-256 signing fingerprints.
4. **Custom Third-Party HTTPS Repositories:** Any repository implementing the F-Droid Index V2 (`entry.jar` / `index-v2.json`) or Index V1 (`index-v1.jar`) standard.

---

## 4. Managing Built-in & Custom F-Droid Repositories (v1.43.1+)

Starting with **v1.43.1**, all built-in and custom F-Droid repositories are managed in one unified bottom sheet in the Setup tab (alongside automatic detection during Obtainium imports):
1. In ApkUp, navigate to **Setup ➔ Update Sources ➔ F-Droid / IzzyOnDroid**.
2. Toggle the source on and tap the row to open the unified **F-Droid Repositories** bottom sheet (`FDroidReposBottomSheet`).
3. Toggle any of the **Built-in Repositories** (*IzzyOnDroid*, *Official F-Droid*, *microG Repo*, *Guardian Project*, or *NewPipe Repo*) or add your own custom HTTPS repository:
   * **Display Name:** Label shown inside ApkUp
   * **Repository URL:** `https://...` endpoint (supports `/repo`, `/archive`, `/fdroid/archive`, or `fdroidrepo://` links with `?fingerprint=…`)
   * **SHA-256 Fingerprint (Optional):** 64-character hex signing fingerprint of the repository index certificate
4. Tap **Add Repository**. ApkUp validates the `https://` host and includes the repository in your next update scan.

---

## 5. Security, Signing Keys & Fingerprint Verification

### Cryptographic JAR Verification & Optional TOFU Pinning
When fetching `entry.jar` (Index V2) or `index-v1.jar` (Index V1 fallback), ApkUp cryptographically verifies the JAR signature (`META-INF/*`) and enforces anti-rollback timestamp checks:
* **Explicitly Pinned Repositories:** Built-in presets and custom repositories with a 64-character SHA-256 fingerprint strictly enforce that exact X.509 signing certificate (fail-closed).
* **Trust-on-First-Use (TOFU) Pinning:** If you add a custom HTTPS repository without specifying a SHA-256 fingerprint, ApkUp verifies the signed `entry.jar` / `index-v1.jar` on the first successful sync, automatically pins its X.509 certificate fingerprint for all future checks, and displays a **TOFU-Pinned** badge in the repository sheet.

### Package Signature Isolation
F-Droid builds packages with its own official signing keys, while developers signing their own releases (or packages from IzzyOnDroid / GitHub) use developer private keys. ApkUp enforces **cryptographic signature matching** before recommending or installing any update to ensure that Android does not reject the package with an `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` error.

---

## Wiki: Authentication Tokens (PAT) for GitHub, GitLab & Codeberg

# 🔑 Configuring GitHub, GitLab & Codeberg Personal Access Tokens

← Back to [Wiki Home](Home) · [Troubleshooting Rate Limits & Auth](Troubleshooting-Source-Errors#3-authentication--rate-limits-http-401-403-429)

By default, ApkUp accesses public developer repositories on GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg / Forgejo anonymously. However, for active users, private repositories, or hosts with strict rate limits, adding your own **Personal Access Token (PAT)** provides maximum reliability.

---

## 📑 Quick Navigation

* [1. Why Do I Need an Access Token?](#1-why-do-i-need-an-access-token)
* [2. How to Generate a GitHub Personal Access Token](#2-how-to-generate-a-github-personal-access-token)
* [3. How to Generate a GitLab Personal Access Token](#3-how-to-generate-a-gitlab-personal-access-token)

* [5. Adding and Testing Tokens in ApkUp](#5-adding-and-testing-tokens-in-apkup)
* [6. Multi-Level GitLab Subgroups (`group/subgroup/project`)](#6-multi-level-gitlab-subgroups-groupsubgroupproject)
* [7. Privacy & Security FAQ](#7-privacy--security-faq)

## 1. Why Do I Need an Access Token?

### GitHub Rate Limits: 60 vs. 5,000 Requests/Hour
GitHub strictly restricts anonymous API requests to **60 requests per hour per public IP address**.
* If you track 15–20 apps hosted on GitHub, checking for updates twice quickly exhausts this quota.
* If you use a VPN or public Wi-Fi, other users sharing that IP also consume your quota, leading to immediate `HTTP 403 API rate limit exceeded` errors.
* Adding a **free** GitHub Personal Access Token raises your limit immediately to **5,000 requests per hour** **and enables batched GitHub GraphQL queries** (checking up to 20 repositories in a single API call instead of one REST request per app).

### GitLab: Private Repositories & Subgroups
While public GitLab projects can often be browsed anonymously, many developers and organizations host repositories under multi-level subgroups or private team workspaces. A GitLab token ensures ApkUp can query release tags and asset URLs reliably.

---

## 2. How to Generate a GitHub Personal Access Token

You can generate a free token in less than 2 minutes:

1. Sign in to your account at **[github.com](https://github.com)**.
2. Click your profile avatar in the top right corner and open **Settings**.
3. In the left sidebar, scroll to the bottom and click **Developer settings**.
4. Select **Personal access tokens** ➔ **Tokens (classic)** (or *Fine-grained tokens*).
5. Click **Generate new token (classic)**:
   * **Note:** Enter a recognizable name (e.g., `ApkUp-Updater`).
   * **Expiration:** Select *No expiration* (or 90/365 days if preferred).
   * **Scopes:** For public repositories, **no scopes are required** (leave all checkboxes unchecked). If you want to track your own private repositories, check `repo`.
6. Click **Generate token** at the bottom of the page.
7. **Important:** Copy the generated token string (`ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx`) immediately. GitHub will never display it again.

---

## 3. How to Generate a GitLab Personal Access Token

1. Sign in to your account at **[gitlab.com](https://gitlab.com)** (or your self-hosted GitLab instance).
2. Click your avatar in the left sidebar and select **Edit profile**.
3. In the left navigation, select **Access Tokens**.
4. Click **Add new token**:
   * **Token name:** `ApkUp-Updater`
   * **Expiration date:** Choose an expiration date.
   * **Select scopes:** Check **`read_api`** (grants read-only access to repository releases and package assets).
5. Click **Create personal access token** and copy the token (`glpat-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx`).

---

## 4. How to Generate a Codeberg / Forgejo Access Token

Starting with **v1.43.0+**, ApkUp supports Codeberg (`codeberg.org`) and self-hosted Forgejo instances via the v1 Releases REST API:

1. Sign in to your account at **[codeberg.org](https://codeberg.org)** (or open **Create token on Codeberg** directly from ApkUp's Codeberg bottom sheet).
2. Navigate to **Settings ➔ Applications** (`https://codeberg.org/user/settings/applications`).
3. Under **Generate New Token**, enter a name (e.g., `ApkUp-Updater`).
4. Select minimal read permissions (`read:repository` for private repos; public repos require no extra scopes).
5. Click **Generate Token** and copy the resulting string into ApkUp.

---

## 5. Adding and Testing Tokens in ApkUp

ApkUp includes a built-in token validator in unified Setup bottom sheets:

1. Open **ApkUp** on your device and go to the **Setup** tab.
2. Enable **GitHub**, **GitLab**, or **Codeberg** and tap the row to open its bottom sheet.
3. Paste your personal access token into the input field.
4. Tap **Test Token** to verify connectivity and inspect remaining API quotas directly before saving.
5. Tap **Save**. Your token is active immediately for both manual and background checks.

---

## 6. Multi-Level GitLab Subgroups (`group/subgroup/project`)

Starting in **ApkUp v1.40.1+**, the GitLab repository resolver supports arbitrary nested subgroup paths.

When linking an app to a GitLab project, you can now enter:
* Standard project: `developer/app-name`
* Subgroup project: `organization/category/app-name`
* Multi-level hierarchy: `enterprise/division/team/mobile/app-name`

ApkUp automatically URL-encodes nested subgroup slugs (`enterprise%2Fdivision%2Fteam%2Fmobile%2Fapp-name`) when querying GitLab REST API v4 endpoints, ensuring releases are fetched accurately without manual configuration.

---

## 7. Privacy & Security FAQ

### Where are my tokens stored?
Your tokens are stored exclusively on your device in Android's private, sandbox-isolated application storage encrypted at rest via **Google Tink (`AES-256-GCM`)** backed by the Android Keystore (`SecurePrefsStore`), with cloud backup disabled (`allowBackup="false"`).

### Does ApkUp transmit my tokens to any third-party server?
**Never.** ApkUp enforces strict host isolation: your GitHub token is sent exclusively to `api.github.com`, your GitLab token exclusively to `gitlab.com`, and your Codeberg token exclusively to `codeberg.org` / `*.codeberg.org` over HTTPS (tokens are stripped automatically on cross-host redirects and are never sent to third-party custom domains). There are no intermediate telemetry, analytics, or proxy servers.

### Can a token be revoked?
Yes, at any time. Simply visit your GitHub, GitLab, or Codeberg token management settings and click **Revoke** or **Delete**.

---

## Wiki: Setting up Shizuku (Quick Guide)

# ⚡ Setting up Shizuku for Silent Updates

[Shizuku](https://shizuku.rikka.app) lets **ApkUp** install updates silently in the background **without Root** — no more tapping "Install" and "Update" on 20 consecutive popups.

This page is the **quick setup checklist**. For the technical architecture, dual-path pipeline, and detailed FAQs, see the full **[Shizuku & Background Installation Guide](https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/wiki/Shizuku-&-Background-Installation)**.

---

## 📑 Quick Navigation

* [1. Why Use Shizuku with ApkUp?](#1-why-use-shizuku-with-apkup)
* [2. Method A: Wireless Debugging (Android 11+, No PC)](#2-method-a-wireless-debugging-android-11-no-pc)
* [3. Method B: PC / Mac (USB ADB)](#3-method-b-pc--mac-usb-adb)
* [4. Method C: Rooted Devices](#4-method-c-rooted-devices)
* [5. Connecting Shizuku in ApkUp](#5-connecting-shizuku-in-apkup)
* [6. Device-Specific Battery & OEM Quirks](#6-device-specific-battery--oem-quirks)

---

## 1. Why Use Shizuku with ApkUp?

* ✅ **One-Tap Batch Updates:** Update all apps with a single tap on *Update All*.
* ✅ **Silent Background Installs:** Scheduled background checks can install updates automatically while your screen is off.
* ✅ **Seamless `.apkm` / Split Bundles:** Multi-part app bundles install cleanly in one session.
* ✅ **Play Store Attribution:** Preserves Play Store installer metadata (`com.android.vending`) so Play Protect and app checks work normally.

---

## 2. Method A: Wireless Debugging (Android 11+, No PC)

1. Install **Shizuku** from Google Play, F-Droid, or [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/RikkaApps/Shizuku/releases).
2. Enable **Developer Options**: **Android Settings ➔ About Phone** ➔ tap **Build Number** 7 times.
3. Connect your phone to Wi-Fi.
4. Open **Shizuku**:
   * Under *Start via Wireless Debugging*, tap **Pairing**.
   * Tap **Developer Options** in the prompt.
   * Enable **Wireless Debugging**, tap its title to open its submenu, and tap **Pair device with pairing code**.
   * Enter the 6-digit code in the Shizuku notification prompt.
5. Return to Shizuku and tap **Start**.

> **Tip:** You only pair once. After a phone reboot, simply open Shizuku and tap **Start** (takes ~3 seconds).

---

## 3. Method B: PC / Mac (USB ADB)

For Android 10 or if Wireless Debugging is unavailable:
1. Enable **USB Debugging** in **Developer Options** and connect via USB.
2. Run the command shown inside Shizuku:
   ```bash
   adb shell sh /sdcard/Android/data/moe.shizuku.privileged.api/start.sh
   ```

---

## 4. Method C: Rooted Devices

If your device uses Magisk, KernelSU, or APatch:
1. Open **Shizuku** ➔ tap **Start (for rooted devices)** and grant superuser permission.
*(Alternatively, ApkUp also supports its own optional **Root Installer (`su`)** under **Setup ➔ Installation & Automation** — see [Section 3.10](https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/wiki/Shizuku-&-Background-Installation#310-optional-root-installer-su-fallback).)*

---

## 5. Connecting Shizuku in ApkUp

1. Open **ApkUp ➔ Setup ➔ Installation & Automation**.
2. Enable **Use Shizuku for background installations**.
3. Tap **Allow all the time** in the Shizuku permission prompt.
4. In **Setup ➔ System & Permissions**, set **Battery Optimization** for both **ApkUp** and **Shizuku** to **Unrestricted** so background updates aren't killed. *(When all system permissions are granted, the permissions card collapses automatically to "All granted" — tap it anytime to inspect.)*

---

## 6. Device-Specific Battery & OEM Quirks

* **Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO (MIUI & HyperOS):**
  * Enable both *USB Debugging* **and** **USB Debugging (Security Settings)** in Developer Options.
  * If the Shizuku pairing code input doesn't expand in the notification, switch **Notification shade** style from *MIUI* to **Android** temporarily.
* **Samsung (One UI):**
  * Set Battery to **Unrestricted** for both **Shizuku** and **ApkUp** under **Settings ➔ Apps**.
* **OnePlus / OPPO / Realme (ColorOS / OxygenOS):**
  * Disable *Auto-freeze* / *Background execution limits* for both **Shizuku** and **ApkUp**.

---

<a id="-part-1-explained-simply-for-everyone-plain-language"></a>
<a name="-part-1-explained-simply-for-everyone-plain-language"></a>
## 🟢 Part 1: Explained Simply for Everyone (Plain Language)

<a id="11-why-does-android-normally-ask-for-confirmation-on-every-update"></a>
<a name="11-why-does-android-normally-ask-for-confirmation-on-every-update"></a>
### 1.1 Why does Android normally ask for confirmation on every update?
For security reasons, Android does not allow regular apps to silently install other apps in the background. If you start 10 updates in an app without special system permissions, Android pops up a confirmation dialog **10 times in a row** (*"Do you want to update this app? [Cancel] [Update]"*). You have to tap every single dialog manually.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="12-what-is-shizuku-and-how-does-it-benefit-me"></a>
<a name="12-what-is-shizuku-and-how-does-it-benefit-me"></a>
### 1.2 What is Shizuku and how does it benefit me?
**[Shizuku](https://shizuku.rikka.app/)** is a free, open-source companion app for Android. It uses an official built-in Android system feature (*Wireless Debugging*) to grant trusted apps like **ApkUp** the exact same installation privileges that normally only the pre-installed Google Play Store has.

**Your benefits with Shizuku in ApkUp:**
- ⚡ **One tap on "Update All" is enough:** All available updates are downloaded and **installed completely automatically in the background**, without you having to tap a single confirmation popup!
- 🛡️ **No Root required:** Your smartphone stays completely unmodified.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="13-step-by-step-guide-setting-up-shizuku-without-root"></a>
<a name="13-step-by-step-guide-setting-up-shizuku-without-root"></a>
### 1.3 Step-by-Step Guide: Setting up Shizuku without Root

> 💡 **New to Shizuku?** For a dedicated, screenshot-friendly beginner walkthrough, see **[Setting up Shizuku](Setting-up-Shizuku)**.
On Android 11 and newer, you can set up Shizuku directly on your phone without a PC (see also the [official Shizuku user guide](https://shizuku.rikka.app/guide/setup/)):

1. **Step 1 – Download Shizuku:**  
   Install the official **Shizuku** app for free from the [Google Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=moe.shizuku.privileged.api) or via [GitHub](https://github.com/RikkaApps/Shizuku/releases).
2. **Step 2 – Enable Developer Options:**  
   Open **Android Settings ➔ About phone**. Tap the **"Build number"** at the bottom **7 times quickly in a row** until you see the message: *"You are now a developer!"*.
3. **Step 3 – Pair Wireless Debugging (one-time setup):**  
   - Connect your phone to a Wi-Fi network.
   - Open the **Shizuku app** and tap **"Pairing"** under *"Start via Wireless debugging"*.
   - Tap the **"Developer options"** button.
   - Scroll down to **"Wireless debugging"**, toggle it on, and tap directly on the text *"Wireless debugging"* to open its sub-menu.
   - Select **"Pair device with pairing code"** and enter the displayed 6-digit code into the Shizuku notification at the top of your screen.
4. **Step 4 – Start Shizuku:**  
   Go back to the Shizuku app and tap **"Start"**. After 2–3 seconds, Shizuku will show *"Shizuku is running"* at the top. *(After that, you can even turn Wi-Fi off again — Shizuku will keep running!)*

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="14-enabling-shizuku-in-apkup-the-3-point-status-check"></a>
<a name="14-enabling-shizuku-in-apkup-the-3-point-status-check"></a>
### 1.4 Enabling Shizuku in ApkUp (The 3-Point Status Check)
Open **ApkUp** and navigate to **Setup ➔ Installation & Automation**. There you will see a clear status indicator with three checkpoints:

| Status Checkpoint | Meaning | What to do if inactive? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Shizuku installed** | Checks whether the Shizuku app is installed on your phone. | Install Shizuku from the [Google Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=moe.shizuku.privileged.api). |
| **2. Service running (Binder)** | Checks whether Shizuku has been started in the background. | Open the Shizuku app and tap *"Start"*. |
| **3. Permission granted** | Checks whether ApkUp is allowed to access Shizuku. | Toggle the switch in ApkUp and tap *"Allow all the time"* in the popup. |

Once all three checkpoints light up green, all installations in ApkUp run completely silently and automatically!

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="15-what-happens-if-my-screen-turns-off-or-i-leave-the-app"></a>
<a name="15-what-happens-if-my-screen-turns-off-or-i-leave-the-app"></a>
### 1.5 What happens if my screen turns off or I leave the app?
Since version **v1.32**, ApkUp includes a dedicated background download service (*Foreground Download Service*):
- When you start a large update or tap *"Update All"*, you can immediately minimize ApkUp, use other apps, or lock your screen.
- In your notification shade, you can always see which app is currently downloading, complete with a percentage progress bar and a **"Cancel"** button.
- **With Shizuku:** Apps finish installing silently even while your screen is turned off.
- **Without Shizuku:** As soon as the background download finishes, ApkUp sends you a notification (*"Ready to install"*) that you simply tap once to confirm.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

<a id="-part-2-technical-documentation-for-experts--power-users"></a>
<a name="-part-2-technical-documentation-for-experts--power-users"></a>
## 💻 Part 2: Technical Documentation for Experts & Power Users

<a id="21-architecture-of-the-dual-path-installation-pipeline"></a>
<a name="21-architecture-of-the-dual-path-installation-pipeline"></a>
### 2.1 Architecture of the Dual-Path Installation Pipeline
To guarantee maximum reliability for both single and batch updates, ApkUp uses a **Dual-Path Strategy with Automatic Fallback**. All installation jobs are processed sequentially through a synchronized queue (Mutex lock):

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Installation Job (Single APK / Split Bundle)"] --> Mutex["Sequential Session Synchronization"]
    Mutex --> CheckPref{"Shizuku Mode Enabled?"}
    
    CheckPref -- "Yes" --> CheckBinder{"Shizuku Binder & Permission Ready?"}
    CheckPref -- "No" --> NativePath["Standard Android PackageInstaller API"]
    
    CheckBinder -- "Ready" --> ShizukuExec["Privileged PackageManager Shell Transaction"]
    CheckBinder -- "Not Ready / Denied" --> FallbackNotice["Notice + Automatic Fallback"]
    
    ShizukuExec --> ShizukuSuccess{"Exit Code == 0 & 'Success'?"}
    ShizukuSuccess -- "Yes" --> Cleanup["Clean Temporary Files & Report Success"]
    ShizukuSuccess -- "No (Error)" --> FallbackNotice
    
    FallbackNotice --> NativePath
    NativePath --> BALCheck{"App in Foreground?"}
    BALCheck -- "Yes" --> DirectDialog["Open System Installer Dialog Immediately"]
    BALCheck -- "No (Background / Lock Screen)" --> HeadsUpNotif["Send High-Priority Install Notification"]
    DirectDialog --> Cleanup
    HeadsUpNotif --> Cleanup
```

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="22-ipc-communication-via-android-binder"></a>
<a name="22-ipc-communication-via-android-binder"></a>
### 2.2 IPC Communication via Android Binder
Communication with the privileged Shizuku server (running under system identity `UID 2000 / shell` or `UID 0 / root`) is performed via Android's Inter-Process Communication (Binder IPC):
- **Package Verification:** Queries the Android `PackageManager` to verify whether `moe.shizuku.privileged.api` is registered on the device.
- **Liveness Check:** Synchronously verifies the remote Binder descriptor (`pingBinder()`) prior to every transaction.
- **Reactive State Events:** System listeners for Binder receipt, Binder death, and permission changes update the UI in real time whenever the Shizuku service starts or stops in the background.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="23-packagemanager-shell-pipeline--play-store-attribution-comandroidvending"></a>
<a name="23-packagemanager-shell-pipeline--play-store-attribution-comandroidvending"></a>
### 2.3 PackageManager Shell Pipeline & Play Store Attribution (`com.android.vending`)
When installing via Shizuku, ApkUp executes a multi-stage transaction against the Android system package manager (`pm`):

1. **Isolated Staging & GZIP Verification:**
   All downloaded package artifacts (single APK, extracted `.apkm` splits, or compressed Google Play splits) are staged in the private app cache and automatically decompressed if a GZIP magic header (`0x1f8b`) is detected.
2. **Session Creation with Play Store Origin:**
   ```bash
   pm install-create -r -i com.android.vending
   ```
   - `-r`: Replaces the existing application while preserving all user data (`INSTALL_REPLACE_EXISTING`).
   - `-i com.android.vending`: Sets the official installation origin (`installerPackageName`) to the Google Play Store. This ensures full compatibility with apps that verify at runtime whether they were installed from an official store source.
3. **Streaming Package Data via Standard Input (`stdin`):**
   For each APK split file, binary data is piped directly through a file descriptor stream into the `pm` process:
   ```bash
   pm install-write -S <byte_size> <session_id> <split_name.apk> -
   ```
   Piping directly over `stdin` cleanly avoids SELinux file access restrictions on private application directories.
4. **Atomic Commit & Rollback Protection:**
   ```bash
   pm install-commit <session_id>
   ```
   If any sub-step fails, the session is cleanly aborted via `pm install-abandon <session_id>` and temporary staging files are purged.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="24-foreground-service--android-14-bal-resilience"></a>
<a name="24-foreground-service--android-14-bal-resilience"></a>
### 2.4 Foreground Service & Android 14+ BAL Resilience
To prevent the Android OS from terminating active downloads when the screen is off or memory pressure is high, ApkUp executes active transfers inside a protected **Android Foreground Service** (`foregroundServiceType="dataSync"`):
- **Lifecycle Management:** The service stays active strictly as long as downloads or installations remain in the queue and stops itself immediately afterward.
- **Protection Against Background Activity Launch (BAL) Restrictions on Android 10–16:**
  When Shizuku is **not** used and a download finishes while ApkUp is in the background, modern Android blocks unsolicited system dialogs from popping up. ApkUp detects this state automatically and dispatches an interactive high-priority notification so the user can launch the Android installer dialog with a single tap at their convenience.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

<a id="-part-3-comprehensive-frequently-asked-questions-faq--common-issues"></a>
<a name="-part-3-comprehensive-frequently-asked-questions-faq--common-issues"></a>
## ❓ Part 3: Comprehensive Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) & Common Issues

<a id="31-do-i-need-root-access-on-my-phone-to-use-shizuku"></a>
<a name="31-do-i-need-root-access-on-my-phone-to-use-shizuku"></a>
### 3.1 Do I need Root access on my phone to use Shizuku?
**No!** Starting with Android 11, Shizuku works completely **without Root** using Android's built-in *Wireless Debugging* feature. However, if your device is rooted (e.g., via Magisk, KernelSU, or APatch), Shizuku can optionally be started directly via Root — which is even faster and requires no pairing code.

---

<a id="32-will-shizuku-void-my-warranty-or-break-banking-apps"></a>
<a name="32-will-shizuku-void-my-warranty-or-break-banking-apps"></a>
### 3.2 Will Shizuku void my warranty or break banking apps?
**No, your warranty remains 100% intact and all banking apps continue to work normally.** Because Shizuku neither unlocks the bootloader nor modifies system partitions (Root), Google's security checks (*Play Integrity / SafetyNet*) and Samsung Knox remain completely untouched.

---

<a id="33-why-do-i-have-to-restart-shizuku-after-rebooting-my-phone"></a>
<a name="33-why-do-i-have-to-restart-shizuku-after-rebooting-my-phone"></a>
### 3.3 Why do I have to restart Shizuku after rebooting my phone?
If your phone is not rooted, Android terminates all debugging services whenever the device is completely powered off or restarted for security reasons.
- You do **not** have to repeat the 6-digit pairing process!
- After rebooting your phone, simply open the Shizuku app and tap **"Start"** once (takes about 3 seconds).

---

<a id="34-issue-wireless-debugging-is-grayed-out-and-cannot-be-turned-on"></a>
<a name="34-issue-wireless-debugging-is-grayed-out-and-cannot-be-turned-on"></a>
### 3.4 Issue: "Wireless debugging" is grayed out and cannot be turned on!
**Cause:** Android only allows enabling *Wireless debugging* while your smartphone is connected to a **Wi-Fi network**.
- **Solution:** Connect your phone briefly to your home Wi-Fi (or a mobile hotspot) and start Shizuku. As soon as Shizuku says *"Shizuku is running"*, you can turn Wi-Fi off again — the service will stay active!

---

<a id="35-issue-shizuku-searches-endlessly-for-the-pairing-service-or-the-code-input-never-appears"></a>
<a name="35-issue-shizuku-searches-endlessly-for-the-pairing-service-or-the-code-input-never-appears"></a>
### 3.5 Issue: Shizuku searches endlessly for the pairing service or the code input never appears!
This behavior occurs most frequently on smartphones from **Xiaomi (MIUI / HyperOS)**, **Oppo/Realme**, and **Samsung**:
1. **Notification Style (Xiaomi):** Go to Android Settings ➔ *Notifications & Control center* ➔ *Notification shade* and switch it from "MIUI" to **"Android"** (Classic). Otherwise, the text box for entering the pairing code inside the notification cannot be expanded.
2. **USB Debugging (Security settings):** On Xiaomi devices, open Developer options and enable **"USB debugging (Security settings)"** in addition to standard *USB debugging*.
3. **Notification Permission:** Make sure you have granted the Shizuku app permission to display notifications.

---

<a id="36-issue-shizuku-stops-by-itself-in-the-background-after-a-while-xiaomi-samsung-oneplus"></a>
<a name="36-issue-shizuku-stops-by-itself-in-the-background-after-a-while-xiaomi-samsung-oneplus"></a>
### 3.6 Issue: Shizuku stops by itself in the background after a while (Xiaomi, Samsung, OnePlus)!
If Shizuku stops after a few hours on its own, this is caused by aggressive OEM battery-saving policies or Android 12/13's *Phantom Process Killer*:
- **Solution 1 (Battery Optimization):** Long-press the **Shizuku** app icon ➔ *App info* ➔ *Battery* and select **"Unrestricted"**.
- **Solution 2 (Developer Options on Android 13+):** In Developer options, enable the toggle **"Disable child process restrictions"**.
- You can also find manufacturer-specific instructions on [DontKillMyApp.com](https://dontkillmyapp.com/).

---

<a id="37-what-happens-if-shizuku-stops-while-apkup-is-downloading-an-update"></a>
<a name="37-what-happens-if-shizuku-stops-while-apkup-is-downloading-an-update"></a>
### 3.7 What happens if Shizuku stops while ApkUp is downloading an update?
ApkUp will not crash and your downloaded update will not be lost! If ApkUp detects that the Shizuku service is unresponsive at the moment of installation, the app **automatically and seamlessly** falls back to the standard Android package installer and shows the regular Android confirmation prompt.

---

<a id="38-does-update-all-also-work-without-shizuku"></a>
<a name="38-does-update-all-also-work-without-shizuku"></a>
### 3.8 Does "Update All" also work without Shizuku?
**Yes, of course.** Even without Shizuku, tapping *"Update All"* downloads all updates in the background. The only difference is that without Shizuku, you briefly tap *"Update"* in the Android system dialog for each downloaded app.

---

<a id="39-why-does-my-phone-recognize-apps-installed-via-shizuku-as-installed-from-google-play-store"></a>
<a name="39-why-does-my-phone-recognize-apps-installed-via-shizuku-as-installed-from-google-play-store"></a>
### 3.9 Why does my phone recognize apps installed via Shizuku as "Installed from Google Play Store"?
This is an intentional feature of ApkUp! When ApkUp installs an app via Shizuku, it passes the parameter `-i com.android.vending` (the official package identifier of the Google Play Store) to Android. Some apps otherwise refuse to run or display warnings if they detect they were updated outside the Play Store. Thanks to this attribution, all updated apps behave as if they came directly from the official store.

---

<a id="310-optional-root-installer-su-fallback"></a>
### 3.10 How does the optional Root Installer (`su`) work alongside Shizuku?
Starting with **v1.43.0+**, rooted devices (Magisk, KernelSU, or APatch) can optionally enable **Root Installer (`su`)** under **Setup ➔ Installation & Automation**:
- **Smart Fallback or Standalone:** When both Shizuku and Root are enabled, ApkUp uses Shizuku first and seamlessly falls back to `su` if Shizuku was not restarted after a reboot. If Shizuku is disabled, ApkUp uses `su` directly for silent foreground and autonomous background updates (while excluding uninstalled Watchlist apps from unattended background installs).
- **Pre-Install Integrity Verification & Origin Preservation:** Before opening a `pm install-create` session, `RootInstaller` verifies all staged base and split APKs via `ApkIntegrityVerifier` (fail-closed) and preserves the existing installer package origin (`-i`).
- **Interactive Root Check Bottom Sheet:** Tapping the **Root Installer (`su`)** row opens the dedicated `RootSetupBottomSheet` where you can verify superuser availability live at any time. For security, importing a configuration backup resets `useRootInstaller` to `false` until you re-enable it on the device.
- **Completely Optional:** On non-rooted phones, keep this option turned off and continue using Shizuku or the normal Android installer.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

- 📖 **Official Shizuku Setup Guide (with screenshots):** [https://shizuku.rikka.app/guide/setup/](https://shizuku.rikka.app/guide/setup/)
- ▶️ **Shizuku on Google Play Store:** [Play Store Link](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=moe.shizuku.privileged.api)

## Wiki: Obtainium Migration & Sync Guide

# 🔄 Obtainium Migration & Sync Guide

ApkUp features native integration with [Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium) JSON exports so you can migrate your tracked apps, custom repository bindings, regex asset filters, and F-Droid repositories in seconds.

---

## 📑 Quick Navigation

* [1. Why Migrate from Obtainium to ApkUp?](#1-why-migrate-from-obtainium-to-apkup)
* [2. How to Export from Obtainium](#2-how-to-export-from-obtainium)
* [3. How to Import into ApkUp (Interactive Preview)](#3-how-to-import-into-apkup-interactive-preview)
* [4. Supported Source Types & Mapping](#4-supported-source-types--mapping)
* [5. Signature Security & Overwrite Protection](#5-signature-security--overwrite-protection)
* [6. ApkUp Settings Backup & Restore](#6-apkup-settings-backup--restore)

---

## 1. Why Migrate from Obtainium to ApkUp?

| Feature | Obtainium | ApkUp |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Multi-Source Aggregation** | Scrapes a single configured URL | Combines Google Play, APKMirror, IzzyOnDroid, F-Droid, GitHub, GitLab & Codeberg |
| **Source Priority & Fallback** | Manual link per app | Global **Source Priority** order + per-app **Source Pinning** with automatic fallback |
| **Cryptographic Signature Defense** | Basic checks | Strict SHA-1 / SHA-256 certificate matching blocks mismatched updates |
| **Direct APKMirror Downloads** | Browser-dependent | In-app resolver with Cloudflare WebView & `.apkm` split bundle extraction |
| **Silent Background Updates** | Notification-driven | Native Shizuku IPC + optional Root (`su`), quiet hours time window & WorkManager |
| **Native UI** | Flutter | 100% native Kotlin / Jetpack Compose Material 3 Expressive |

---

## 2. How to Export from Obtainium

1. Open **Obtainium** on your Android device.
2. Tap **Settings ➔ Import / Export**.
3. Tap **Export Apps to JSON File** and save `obtainium_export.json` (e.g. to *Downloads*).

---

## 3. How to Import into ApkUp (Interactive Preview)

1. Open **ApkUp ➔ Setup ➔ Backup & Restore ➔ Obtainium Import**.
2. Select your `obtainium_export.json` file in Android's file picker.
3. Review everything in the **Interactive Preview Sheet** before applying:
   * **Repo Links for Installed Apps:** Matches installed package IDs to GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg/Forgejo, and `apkFilterRegEx` rules.
   * **Third-Party F-Droid Repositories:** Detects custom HTTPS `/repo` or `/archive` URLs (including 64-character `?fingerprint=` pins) and imports them into ApkUp's unified F-Droid manager.
   * **Watch Uninstalled Apps (Opt-In):** Lists uninstalled apps from the export (unchecked by default so you only add what you explicitly select to your **Watchlist**).
4. Tap **Import selected**, then pull to refresh on the **Updates** tab!

---

## 4. Supported Source Types & Mapping

* **GitHub Repositories:** Mapped to ApkUp's GitHub resolver (standard releases, pre-releases, and asset regex matching).
* **GitLab Projects:** Mapped to ApkUp's GitLab resolver (including multi-level subgroups and self-hosted hosts).
* **Codeberg & Forgejo Repositories:** Mapped to ApkUp's Codeberg/Forgejo v1 resolver (`codeberg.org` and self-hosted Forgejo).
* **F-Droid & IzzyOnDroid Links:** Mapped to ApkUp's Index V2 streaming engine and F-Droid repository list.
* **APK Filter Regex (`apkFilterRegEx`):** Automatically preserved from Obtainium entries.

---

## 5. Signature Security & Overwrite Protection

Even when a custom repository offers a higher `versionCode`, ApkUp extracts the signing certificate from the downloaded APK and verifies it against the currently installed app before installation. Mismatches are flagged immediately to prevent `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` errors.

---

## 6. ApkUp Settings Backup & Restore

To back up or transfer your **ApkUp** configuration (including custom repo links, ignored apps, source priority, and preferences) to another phone via Android's Storage Access Framework (SAF), follow the full guide:
👉 **[Guide: Backing up settings and restoring them on a new phone](https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/wiki/App-Management,-Filters,-Background-Checks-&-Backup#16-guide-backing-up-settings-and-restoring-them-on-a-new-phone)**

*(Note: Personal Access Tokens are stored encrypted on-device via Google Tink `AES-256-GCM` and are never exported in plaintext JSON backups.)*

---

This guide explains how to skip faulty updates, ignore apps, track uninstalled apps via your Watchlist, export APKs, schedule background update windows, use rollback backups, opt into ApkUp beta updates, and transfer your configuration between devices.

<a id="-part-1-explained-simply-for-everyone"></a>
## 🟢 Part 1: Explained Simply for Everyone

<a id="11-skip-this-version-vs-ignore-app-permanently"></a>
### 1.1 "Skip this version" vs. "Ignore app permanently"
| Feature | What happens? | When will you be notified again? | How to undo? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **⏭️ Skip this version** | Hides only **that specific build** (e.g. `2.4.1`). | Automatically as soon as a **newer version** (`2.4.2`) is released. | **Setup ➔ Manage skipped versions** |
| **🙈 Ignore app permanently** | Excludes the app from all future update checks. | Never — until you unhide it. | **Setup ➔ Manage ignored apps** or **Apps ➔ Ignored** chip |

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="12-search-sorting-watchlist--app-watcher-import"></a>
### 1.2 Search, Sorting, Watchlist & App Watcher Import
* **Instant Search & Sorting:** Both **Updates** and **Apps** offer live search and flexible sorting (*Name A–Z / Z–A*, *Source*, *Newest Release Date* in Updates, *Recently Updated* in Apps) with automatic scroll-to-top.
* **Watchlist (Uninstalled Apps):** Tap **`+`** in the **Apps** top bar to follow an uninstalled app by package ID (and optional GitHub/GitLab/Codeberg URL). Tracked entries appear under the **Watched** chip and surface new releases in **Updates** with a **`Watched · New`** badge and a direct **Install** button.
* **Import from App Watcher:** Open **Setup ➔ Import & Export ➔ Import from App Watcher** to import uninstalled apps (including their last-seen version) straight into your Watchlist.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="13-saving-apks-batch-eta--offline-diagnostic-logs"></a>
### 1.3 Saving APKs, Batch ETA & Offline Diagnostic Logs
* **Save APK without Installing:** Tap **Save APK** inside any update card to export standalone `.apk` files or `.apks` split archives into `Download/ApkUp/` (or a custom SAF folder via **Setup ➔ Saved APK folder**). File/archive/SHA-256 integrity is verified even if the installed app has a different signing certificate.
* **Overall Batch Progress & ETA:** Batch updates and exports display combined progress percentage, speed, and estimated time remaining.
* **Offline Diagnostic & Update Log:** Under **Setup ➔ Advanced Settings ➔ Diagnostic & Update Log**, export (`.txt`) or share a sanitized report. Optional process `logcat` is **disabled by default (opt-in)** and all tokens/credentials (`Bearer`, `ghp_`, `glpat-`, `PRIVATE-TOKEN`, Aurora `Auth=`/`aas_et/`) are redacted automatically.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="14-background-checks-time-window-pre-releases--rollbacks"></a>
### 1.4 Background Checks, Time Window, Pre-Releases & Rollbacks
* **Background Check Interval:** Under **Setup ➔ Automatic Checks & Schedule**, choose **6 hours**, **12 hours**, **24 hours** (recommended), **48 hours**, or **7 days**.
* **Background Update Time Window:** Enable **Background Update Time Window** to either pause checks & auto-updates during quiet hours (e.g. `22:00 – 07:00`) or restrict them to an active window. Any run that falls outside the window automatically schedules a one-time catch-up at the next window start.
* **Pre-Release Channels (Apps):** Open **Setup ➔ Include Pre-Releases** to enable **Beta**, **RC**, **Alpha**, or **Nightly** channels globally, or override pre-releases per app.
* **ApkUp Self-Updater Beta Opt-In:** Under **Setup ➔ About ➔ Receive beta updates** (disabled by default), you can opt into pre-release builds of ApkUp itself. Pre-releases show a **Beta / Pre-Release** badge in the update dialog and enforce identical SHA-256 and certificate checks; turning it off automatically returns you to stable with the next regular release.
* **Automatic Rollback Backups & Update History:** Keep backups of previous APKs in private storage (`2 GB` LRU limit) before updating so you can roll back anytime from **Update History** (in-place via Root `-r -d`, or guided two-step rollback without Root).

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="15-showing-or-hiding-system-apps"></a>
### 1.5 Showing or Hiding System Apps
ApkUp hides pre-installed system apps by default so your list stays clean. To include system components (such as *Android System WebView*), enable **Setup ➔ Include System Apps**.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="16-guide-backing-up-settings-and-restoring-them-on-a-new-phone"></a>
### 1.6 Guide: Backing up settings and restoring them on a new phone
* **📤 Export Configuration:** **ApkUp ➔ Setup ➔ Backup & Restore ➔ Export Configuration** ➔ save `apkup-backup.json` to Downloads or cloud storage.
* **📥 Import Configuration:** **ApkUp ➔ Setup ➔ Backup & Restore ➔ Import Configuration** ➔ select your `.json` file. All sources, custom source priority, pinned apps, filters, pre-release settings, and repo links are restored immediately.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="-part-2-technical-documentation-for-experts--power-users"></a>
## 💻 Part 2: Technical Documentation for Experts & Power Users

<a id="21-filter-architecture-package-wide-exclusion-vs-version-pinning"></a>
### 2.1 Filter Architecture: Package-Wide Exclusion vs. Version Pinning
1. **Package-Wide Exclusion (Ignore App):** Applied **before** network requests are dispatched — reduces payload size, saves GitHub API quota, and preserves privacy.
2. **Version-Specific Pinning (Skip Version):** Stores `(packageName, version, versionCode)` and expires automatically as soon as any source delivers a strictly higher `versionCode`.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="22-battery-friendly-background-scheduling-via-android-workmanager"></a>
### 2.2 Battery-Friendly Background Scheduling via Android `WorkManager`
ApkUp delegates background checks to Android **`WorkManager`** (`NetworkType.CONNECTED`), batching work into OS maintenance windows (Doze / App Standby) with atomic `.part` download staging.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="23-persistent-update-snapshot-cache-for-instant-app-startup"></a>
### 2.3 Persistent Update Snapshot Cache for Instant App Startup
After each scan, ApkUp stores a local **Update Snapshot** in private app storage and reconciles it against live `PackageManager` state on launch so the **Updates** tab populates instantaneously without forcing a redundant online scan.

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="24-structure--privacy-of-the-json-backup-file-saf"></a>
### 2.4 Structure & Privacy of the JSON Backup File (SAF)
ApkUp uses Android's **Storage Access Framework (SAF)** with zero broad storage permissions. The exported JSON contains:
- Enabled update sources, source priority order, pinned app sources, F-Droid repositories, and watched apps
- Ignored package names, skipped versions, and custom GitHub/GitLab/Codeberg bindings (validated on import for `https://`, allowed hosts, and regex limits)
- Theme, display, update window, pre-release channels, rollback backup toggle, self-updater beta opt-in (`includeSelfUpdatePreReleases`, safely defaulting to `false` on older backups), and background check preferences

*(Note: Personal Access Tokens remain encrypted on-device in Google Tink `AES-256-GCM` storage and are never exported in plaintext backups; importing a backup also resets `useRootInstaller` to `false` with a security notice.)*

[⬆️ Back to Table of Contents](#-table-of-contents)

---

<a id="-part-3-frequently-asked-questions-faq"></a>
## ❓ Part 3: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

<a id="31-when-should-i-use-skip-this-version-vs-ignore-app-permanently"></a>
### 3.1 When should I use "Skip this version" vs. "Ignore app permanently"?
Use **Skip this version** for one buggy release you want to jump past; use **Ignore app permanently** when you intentionally want to stay on an older or customized build forever.

<a id="32-why-should-i-be-careful-with-system-apps"></a>
### 3.2 Why should I be careful with System Apps?
OEM system apps (Phone, Camera, Gallery, Launcher) are often tied to specific device models and firmware. Updating them from generic mirror builds can cause crashes.

<a id="33-do-background-update-checks-drain-the-battery"></a>
### 3.3 Do background update checks drain the battery?
**No.** `WorkManager` runs brief 3–5 second checks inside existing OS network wakeups.

<a id="34-why-am-i-not-receiving-background-notifications"></a>
### 3.4 Why am I not receiving background notifications?
1. Check **Android Settings ➔ Apps ➔ ApkUp ➔ Notifications** (Android 13+ permission).
2. Set **Android Settings ➔ Apps ➔ ApkUp ➔ Battery** to **Unrestricted** (especially on Xiaomi, Samsung, and OnePlus).

<a id="35-why-does-a-skipped-version-reappear-after-a-hotfix"></a>
### 3.5 Why does a skipped version reappear after a hotfix?
"Skip this version" tracks the internal `versionCode`. If the developer ships a hotfix with the same display name (e.g. `2.1.0`) but a higher `versionCode`, ApkUp rightly surfaces the newer build.

<a id="36-does-the-json-backup-include-apk-files-or-tokens-and-can-i-edit-it"></a>
### 3.6 Does the JSON backup include APK files or tokens, and can I edit it?
No — the `.json` file is only a few KB of settings (no APKs, no secret tokens). You can edit it safely in any text editor; just avoid trailing commas (`,`) before `}` or `]`.

---

<a id="-part-4-official-links--further-resources"></a>
## 🔗 Part 4: Official Links & Further Resources

- 🔋 **[Don't Kill My App!](https://dontkillmyapp.com/)** — OEM guides to keep background checks reliable.
- ⚙️ **[Android WorkManager Docs](https://developer.android.com/topic/libraries/architecture/workmanager)** — Official background scheduling architecture.
- 🔄 **[Obtainium Migration & Sync Guide](https://github.com/DurchEins/apkup/wiki/Obtainium-Migration-&-Sync-Guide)** — Migrate your Obtainium JSON export into ApkUp.
